items.q: Spherocytes, raised MCHC, negative Coombs, splenomegaly and affected father most likely indicate what?
items.exp: Dominant membrane protein defects sphere red cells destroyed in spleen with negative immune testing and family history. Autoimmune disease matches morphology but Coombs is positive without this inheritance.
r: Incorrect. Immune disease is Coombs positive.
Correct. Inherited spheres with negative Coombs mean spherocytosis.
Incorrect. G6PD causes episodic bite cells, not chronic spheres.
Incorrect. Thalassaemia shows microcytic targets and Hb changes.
items.kp: Family spheres plus negative Coombs equals membrane defect.

items.q: Heinz bodies and bite cells after primaquine in a man with dark urine indicate deficiency of what?
items.exp: G6PD deficiency fails glutathione defence so oxidant drugs denature haemoglobin into Heinz bodies splenically bitten into bite cells, with intravascular haemolysis. Screening before primaquine or rasburicase prevents crises.
r: Incorrect. Kinase deficiency is chronic without drug bursts.
Correct. Oxidant burst plus Heinz bodies means G6PD deficiency.
Incorrect. Spectrin loss spheres cells chronically.
Incorrect. Nucleotidase deficiency stipples cells chronically rarely.
items.kp: Oxidant drug plus bite cells: G6PD deficiency. Screen first.

items.q: Why can G6PD assay falsely appear normal during an acute haemolytic crisis?
o: Older deficient cells destroyed; surviving reticulocytes have higher enzyme
items.exp: The most deficient old cells haemolyse first, leaving young reticulocytes with near normal activity that masks deficiency. Repeat assay two to three months later for truth.
r: Incorrect. No induction occurs; cell selection explains it.
Correct. Young survivors falsely normalise the assay.
Incorrect. Assays measure enzyme activity directly.
Incorrect. Coombs tests antibody, unrelated to enzyme levels.
items.kp: Test G6PD between crises, never during one.

items.q: Dark morning urine, venous thrombosis in unusual sites and pancytopenia suggest which acquired disorder?
o: Paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria (PIGA, lost CD55 CD59)
items.exp: PNH clones lose GPI anchored CD55 and CD59, suffering complement intravascular haemolysis (dark first urine), hypercoagulable thromboses (hepatic veins) and aplastic overlap. Flow cytometry proves anchor loss.
r: Incorrect. Spherocytosis is chronic splenic childhood disease.
Correct. Anchor loss triad means PNH.
Incorrect. G6PD bursts episodically without thrombosis pancytopenia.
Incorrect. Trait is asymptomatic without this triad.
items.kp: Haemolysis plus clots plus empty marrow equals PNH.

items.q: Splenectomy in hereditary spherocytosis achieves what?
o: Stops haemolysis and anaemia though spherocytes persist
Cures gallstone risk permanently in all
items.exp: Removing the destroying spleen normalises red survival and haemoglobin despite persistent spherocytes, at the cost of lifelong encapsulated organism sepsis risk needing vaccination and prophylaxis planning.
r: Incorrect. Membrane defect and spheres remain for life.
Correct. Haemolysis stops; shape persists.
Incorrect. Existing stones and risk need separate care.
Incorrect. Parvovirus still arrests marrow production.
items.kp: Splenectomy cures destruction, not the sphere.

items.q: Chronic haemolysis with echinocytes (burr cells), splenomegaly and iron overload without transfusions suggests deficiency of what?
items.exp: Pyruvate kinase deficiency depletes ATP, rigidifying red cells into echinocytes for chronic splenic haemolysis from childhood, with gallstones and transfusional independent iron loading.
r: Incorrect. G6PD haemolyses episodically after triggers.
Correct. ATP starved chronic haemolysis means pyruvate kinase lack.
Incorrect. Ankyrin loss spheres cells dominantly.
Incorrect. Band 3 defects sphere or oval cells, not this energy picture.
items.kp: Lifelong haemolysis without triggers: think pyruvate kinase.

items.q: Favism (haemolysis after broad beans) occurs in deficiency of which enzyme?
items.exp: Fava bean oxidants (vicine) overwhelm G6PD deficient glutathione defence, haemolysing red cells especially in Mediterranean and Asian variants. Families must avoid beans, naphthalene and trigger drugs.
r: Incorrect. Hexokinase deficiency is rare chronic haemolysis.
Correct. Favism is G6PD deficiency unmasked.
Incorrect. Kinase deficiency is trigger independent chronic.
Incorrect. Synthetase defects are rarer systemic diseases.
items.kp: Beans plus burst cells equals G6PD favism.

items.q: Warm autoimmune haemolysis (IgG, Coombs positive) most associates with which underlying group?
o: Lymphoproliferative disease, lupus and drugs such as methyldopa
items.exp: Warm IgG coats red cells for splenic Fc removal, secondary to CLL and lymphoma, lupus or drugs, responding to steroids and treating the cause. Cold disease is IgM complement mediated instead.
r: Incorrect. Trigger drugs cause G6PD bursts Coombs negative.
Correct. Lymphoma, lupus and drugs drive warm immune haemolysis.
Incorrect. Spectrin mutation is hereditary Coombs negative.
Incorrect. Iron lack causes microcytosis without haemolysis.
items.kp: Warm Coombs haemolysis: hunt lymphoma, lupus and drugs.

items.q: Cold agglutinin disease with acrocyanosis after mycoplasma infection works through which immunoglobulin and mechanism?
o: IgM fixing complement, agglutinating in cold peripheries
items.exp: Cold IgM agglutinates red cells in cool fingers and fixes complement (C3d Coombs pattern), haemolysing on rewarming, after mycoplasma or EBV or in lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma. Warmth is therapy.
r: Incorrect. That describes warm disease mechanics.
Correct. IgM complement cold agglutination.
Incorrect. IgA deficiency does not haemolyse this way.
Incorrect. IgE mediates allergy, not agglutinin haemolysis.
items.kp: Cold fingers clump first: IgM cold agglutinins.

items.q: Pigment gallstones in a haemolytic child are composed mainly of what?
o: Calcium bilirubinate from excess unconjugated bilirubin
items.exp: Chronic haemolysis floods bile with unconjugated bilirubin precipitating calcium bilirubinate black pigment stones, even in childhood spherocytosis or sickle disease, unlike cholesterol stones of obesity.
r: Incorrect. Cholesterol stones follow bile supersaturation states.
Correct. Bilirubin pigment stones follow haemolysis.
Incorrect. Oxalate stones are renal, not gallbladder pigment.
Incorrect. Struvite infects urinary tracts.
items.kp: Haemolysis stones the gallbladder black with bilirubin.
